findings.title: canManage() grants manage rights to callers who only have VIEW on groups
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. Because of this, an admin with only an all-groups `view` permission is treated as able to manage all groups.

`canManage()` guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`requireManage()`). As a result, a read-only group admin can create top-level groups and move existing groups to the top level.

This is a privilege escalation. Only the `MANAGE` scope should be checked here. The interface javadoc repeats the same mistake and should be corrected too.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs, not group IDs, and searches by the wrong type
findings.body:
The method iterates `findByType(server, "Groups")`. Per-group resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never get a type set, so they are not found. Only the all-groups "Groups" resource has this type.

It then calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. That method does `findByName(server, groupId)`, but resource names are group IDs, not resource IDs. The lookup therefore always falls back to the all-groups resource.

Finally, it adds `groupResource.getId()` (an authorization resource ID) to the result set, which callers treat as group IDs. The set is passed to `UserModel.GROUPS` session filtering in `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` and to `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`. Possible effects:
- user search is constrained to a nonexistent group ID, so no users are returned;
- counts are wrong;
- pagination breaks, because filtering otherwise happens only post-query.

The method should iterate the group resources (by name) and return `resource.getName()`.

findings.title: Group removal listener now calls a V2 method that throws UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body:
`MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

The listener registered here calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on every `GroupRemovedEvent`. When V2 is enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`. Previously V2 used the V1 `GroupPermissions` here, so this path did not throw.

If both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled, deleting a group will now fail. The listener should skip V2, or the V2 implementation should be a no-op.

findings.title: Wrong javadoc for requireManageMembers
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. It actually delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, so the reference is wrong and misleading.

findings.title: Public utility method removed without deprecation
findings.body:
The public static method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes` is removed outright. `ModelToRepresentation` is a utility class that custom extensions can call, so any extension using this method will break at compile or link time.

Consider deprecating the method first and removing it later.
